annotations.title: Start a Chorus book, and get the one link to forward.

description: Starts a book of voice, video and written messages and returns the single link the organiser sends to everyone taking part. The book is for one person or a couple, or it is called by a title when it is for nobody in particular: a family’s recipes, a class’s year, a team’s goodbye. Start the simplest book that fits what the person said and hand over the link straight away. Gathering is free and the people recording need no app and no account. Leave organiser_email out and the book is made at once with nobody signing in: hand over the collecting link, and keep_link for later, when they want to read the messages in Chorus, have Chorus email people or order the book. With organiser_email, the first call emails them a six digit code and the second call, with the code, makes the book in their account.

answer_with.description: Any of voice, video and written. Voice and written when not said.

closes_on.description: The day collecting stops, as 2026-11-14. Allow three weeks before the day if a printed copy is wanted.

code.description: The six digit code emailed to the organiser. Leave it out on the first call to have one sent.

expecting.description: Who is expected to record, by name or role, so book_status can say who is still out. Never email addresses.

lead_with.description: Which of those is the big button on a contributor’s phone.

occasion.description: A big birthday, A wedding, A new baby, As they grow, In memory, or Something else. Plain words are matched to one of those.

organiser_email.description: Leave this out to start the book with no sign-in. Give it only when the organiser wants the book in their Chorus account now; they then get in with a six digit code.

questions.description: The questions everybody is asked, up to 12, written from what the person told you, each one line of up to 200 characters that a person can answer out loud in a minute or two. In a book with subject_name, {name} in a question becomes that name. When this is left out, a book with subject_name gets the set for the occasion and a book with only a title gets three open questions.

steps.description: What each person is asked, in order, one screen each, when the book needs more than questions. Each step is { kind, text }: words (a question answered by voice, video or writing, text required), song (they search for it or paste a Spotify, YouTube or Apple Music link; it prints as the page's heading with a code that plays it), photo, voice (a voice note that prints as a code on their page), date, choice (with choices, two to eight), link (prints as a code), name (who it is from; asked first when left out). text is what the screen asks, with {name} for the person; leave it out for a song, photo, voice or name and Chorus asks it. optional: false makes a photo, voice, date, choice or link one they cannot skip. Each person's answers make one page. Steps outrank questions. Example for a song book: [{kind:'song'},{kind:'words',text:'Why does it remind you of {name}?'},{kind:'photo'},{kind:'voice'},{kind:'name'}].

subject_name.description: Who the book is for, when it is for one person or a couple, as the organiser says it, for example Mum. Give subject_name, title or both. A book for one person needs only subject_name.

title.description: What the book is called, in the person’s words, for example The Kelly family recipes. One line, up to 40 characters.
